newsitem.title: JAPAN: Toyota says to become more environment conscious.
newsitem.headline: Toyota says to become more environment conscious.

text.p: Toyota Motor Corp., Japan's top car maker, pledged Wednesday to offer automobiles that are more friendly to the environment.
"From this year, I promise we will commit ourselves even more strongly to environmental issues," Toyota President Hiroshi Okuda said at a forum on Toyota's involvement in environmental issues.
Last week in California Toyota said it would start marketing its RAV4-EV electric vehicle, with a suggested retail price of $42,000.
"In our company management issues, Toyota has given top priority to conserving the environment. The reduction of car emissions is the responsibility of car makers," Okuda said.
"Toyota will make utmost efforts to try to drastically reduce emissions of carbon dioxide, hydrocarbons, carbon monoxide and nitrogen oxides."

In one or two years, Toyota plans to launch a vehicle equipped with a new diesel engine that improves fuel efficiency by 25 percent compared with conventional diesel engines, Toyota Executive Vice President Akihiro Wada said.
Wada also said Toyota will introduce a "hybrid" car powered by gasoline and batteries within this year.
The fuel consumption of hybrid cars is half of that of Toyota's popular Corolla model, while emissions are one-tenth, he said.
In June, Toyota said it would build an assembly line for its "hybrid" car in central Japan.
